Summary: Add FCM configuration and startup validation
Description: Add FCM_ENABLED, FCM_PROJECT_ID, FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL, FCM_PRIVATE_KEY, optional FCM_WEB_VAPID_KEY, and startup validation in messaging-service/backend.
Acceptance Criteria: Service boots when FCM_ENABLED=false; fails fast with clear errors when enabled and misconfigured; env vars documented in templates and ops docs.

Summary: Create FCM device token table + migration
Description: Add token persistence model with actor_type, actor_id, event_id, platform, token, status, metadata, and timestamps.
Dependencies: Add FCM configuration and startup validation
Acceptance Criteria: Migration applies cleanly in dev/staging/prod; duplicate active tokens are prevented; soft-revocation supported.

Summary: Extend delivery logging for fcm channel
Description: Reuse existing delivery log model and add fcm channel conventions, provider_message_id, and normalized statuses.
Dependencies: Create FCM device token table + migration
Acceptance Criteria: Each FCM send attempt creates a delivery record; statuses include queued/sent/failed/invalid_token; non-FCM logging unchanged.

Description: Add authenticated endpoint to register token and device metadata, with idempotent upsert behavior.
Dependencies: Create FCM device token table + migration
Acceptance Criteria: Registering same token multiple times does not duplicate active rows; actor and platform fields are stored; endpoint returns current state.

Summary: Unregister or revoke FCM token API
Description: Add authenticated endpoint to deactivate token for current user/guest session.
Acceptance Criteria: Revocation is idempotent; revoked tokens are excluded from sends; revoked_at and updated_at are written.

Description: Handle token changes by replacing old active token for same device identity.
Acceptance Criteria: New token becomes active; previous token is revoked; duplicate notifications do not occur after refresh.

Description: Add PushProvider interface and implementations for existing web push and FCM to avoid channel-specific branching in callers.
Dependencies: Extend delivery logging for fcm channel
Acceptance Criteria: Existing browser push remains functional; FCM provider can be toggled; callers use abstraction only.

Summary: Implement FCM sender client + error mapping
Description: Build sender with canonical handling for retryable and permanent FCM errors, including invalid token outcomes.
Acceptance Criteria: Retryable errors are retried; permanent token failures mark token invalid; provider_message_id and error codes are logged.

Description: Introduce push.send queue job with idempotency key, retries, and dead-letter handling.
Dependencies: Implement FCM sender client + error mapping
Acceptance Criteria: Queue-backed async send path works end-to-end; duplicate jobs are deduped; dead jobs are inspectable and replayable.

Summary: iOS platform bootstrap for FCM token registration
Description: Add the Capacitor iOS platform (Android-only today) and link it to APNs via Firebase so an iOS build can obtain an FCM device token. FCM delivery itself is already platform-unified — one send call reaches Android/iOS/web alike — this ticket is only the missing client-side prerequisite (Xcode project, APNs auth key uploaded to the Firebase project, Capacitor iOS push plugin) needed before any iOS device can register a token. No server-side dispatch changes.
Acceptance Criteria: npx cap add ios project exists and builds; APNs auth key is uploaded to the Firebase project; a physical or simulator iOS build registers an FCM token through the same register-token API Android uses; no changes required to server-side dispatch.

Description: Request notification permissions, obtain FCM token, and call register API on login/session restore.
Acceptance Criteria: First login registers token; permission-denied path is handled gracefully; token registration telemetry is emitted.

Summary: Mobile token refresh and logout revocation
Description: Send refreshed tokens automatically and revoke token on logout.
Acceptance Criteria: Token refresh updates backend without duplicates; logout revokes token; stale token stops receiving pushes.

Description: Implement app behavior for foreground banners, background receipt, and tap-to-open deep links.
Acceptance Criteria: Foreground notifications show in-app UX; tapping background notifications deep-links correctly; killed-app open path lands on destination.

Description: Keep current VAPID web push path in first release and document if/when to unify web on FCM.
Acceptance Criteria: No regression to existing browser push; architecture decision record is published with rationale and follow-up steps.

Description: Wire event announcement publish flow to push dispatch for eligible recipients.
Acceptance Criteria: Audience filters are enforced server-side; payload is safe/minimal; delivery logs include fcm outcomes.

Summary: Guest chat and host reply alerts
Description: Wire guest chat/direct host reply flows to push dispatch using private-safe payload strategy.
Acceptance Criteria: Private notifications do not expose message bodies by default; open-time auth re-check is required; no cross-thread leakage.

Description: Build a net-new staff/organizer push channel: today's push path (GuestPushSubscription, send_event_push) is guest-only, so this needs its own device-token actor scope (actor_type=staff) and a new recipient-resolution path off EventUser/role assignment rather than Guest — not just a new notification class layered on an existing staff channel, because none exists yet.
Acceptance Criteria: Staff device tokens register under actor_type=staff; recipients are resolved via EventUser role assignment, not Guest; only assigned staff for scanner/check-in workflows receive alerts; feature can be toggled per event; incorrect role recipients are blocked.

Description: Add per-user/guest push preferences by category, including sensible defaults.
Acceptance Criteria: Preferences are saved and enforced at dispatch; defaults are documented; updates apply without restart.

Description: Add quiet-hours evaluation for non-urgent pushes using event or user timezone.
Acceptance Criteria: Non-urgent pushes are suppressed in quiet window; urgent classes can bypass with explicit policy; behavior is auditable.

Description: Add per-event and per-actor push throttles with circuit-breaker style protection.
Acceptance Criteria: Burst spam is throttled; throttling metrics are emitted; critical system notifications are not starved.

Description: Add dashboards for token health, send success by platform, invalid token trend, queue depth, and latency.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard panels exist and are populated in staging; key KPIs are visible per environment and event cohort.

Description: Add alerts for failure spikes, queue backlog, and invalid-token surges with operator runbook.
Acceptance Criteria: Alerts fire in test scenarios; runbook includes triage, rollback, and replay instructions; ownership is assigned.

Description: Implement secret handling, redaction, and rotation procedure for FCM credentials.
Dependencies: Add FCM configuration and startup validation
Acceptance Criteria: No raw private key values appear in logs; rotation is documented and tested; least privilege is enforced.

Description: Add kill switch and cohort-based enablement for FCM by environment and event groups.
Acceptance Criteria: Global kill switch works instantly; cohort targeting works for canary events; fallback to existing channels remains intact.

Description: Run mobile/web/platform scenarios: permission states, foreground/background, token rotation, privacy, and delivery outcomes.
Acceptance Criteria: QA pass report covers Android/iOS/web baseline; privacy tests pass; known issues are tracked with severity.

Description: Execute staged rollout: internal events, limited canary events, then broader expansion based on KPI thresholds.
Acceptance Criteria: Canary KPIs meet success thresholds; go/no-go checklist is completed; staged expansion plan is approved.
